tasks.short: Establish cost codes, controls, reporting views and procedures for monitoring project costs.

steps.what: Agree reporting needs, cost ownership, thresholds and review frequency.
Document cost definitions, source fields, allocation rules and reporting responsibilities.
Reconcile sample transactions and commitments against project budgets using exports.
Configure cost views, refresh schedules, access and exception alerts.
Write operating procedures for refreshes, corrections, escalation and reporting.
Test sample periods, access restrictions, totals and alert behaviour.
Approve cost definitions, reporting controls and release readiness.
Activate approved reporting views and publish the operating procedure.

tasks.design: Configure project cost views in the {ERP} and {BI}, using a reusable mapping register in the {WORKFLOW} and validated imports from the {PROCUREMENT} and {PROJECT}. A deterministic job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} checks totals and generates procedures from approved fields; release follows the financial controller's approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost definitions differed across teams. Mapping, reconciliation and control documentation required repeated specialist effort even where reporting features already existed.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration handles most reporting. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building import adapters, reconciliation checks and procedure templates; it does not settle accounting definitions.
tasks.still_hard: Allocating shared costs, distinguishing commitments from actuals and keeping historical comparisons consistent after code changes.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which cost signals justify intervention and negotiate definitions that project and finance teams can both use.

ambition.what: A reusable cost-monitoring starter package for small project teams.

tasks.altitude: The estimator spends more time testing whether reports expose useful decisions and less time assembling reporting infrastructure. They can lead monitoring design; financial control approval remains with the financial controller.

reach.learn: Data grain, refresh lineage, access controls and reconciliation tests.

reach.task: Reconcile project costs to the general ledger.
reach.learn: Accruals, allocation methods and period-close controls.

evidence.claim: Configured reporting, mapping registers and deterministic reconciliation are plausible building blocks; the digest provides no estimator-specific implementation case.
Build ranges and remaining-time estimates are planning hypotheses, not measured results.

assumptions: The baseline combines existing financial reports with manual mapping and control documentation.
The first release covers one project-cost model and a limited set of source feeds.
Time shares describe setup effort, not recurring report production.
The design needs no model loop when definitions and procedure fields are structured.
unknowns: Which reporting features and configuration rights are already available?
Are cost codes and project identifiers consistent across source systems?
Who can approve allocation rules and production configuration?
Will reporting expose individual employee costs or performance?
Which national consultation requirements and internal access reviews apply?
research_questions: Which native reporting features can replace custom development?
Which sample periods best reveal commitment duplication, late postings and allocation errors?
new_work: Maintain cost mappings and source-field contracts.
Investigate failed reconciliations and stale feeds.
Update procedures when controls or responsibilities change.

tasks.short: Compare internal production costs with supplier offers and recommend whether to make or buy.

steps.what: Review specifications, quantities, quality requirements and delivery dates.
Confirm material needs, labour hours, capacity and feasible production routes.
Request comparable supplier quotations and clarify scope.
Read quotations and identify price breaks, exclusions, tooling charges and delivery terms.

loop.input: Supplier quotes, comparison scope and a fixed quotation-field schema.
loop.output: Quote fields with page references, units, validity dates and unresolved exclusions.
loop.check: Validate required fields, currencies, units and price arithmetic; the estimator approves extracted terms before calculation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per quote; ambiguous or missing terms enter manual clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents express exclusions and commercial terms in varying free text. Structured portal fields should bypass the loop.

steps.what: Calculate comparable costs and test demand, utilisation, scrap and delivery scenarios.
Recommend an option, explaining capacity opportunity costs and supply risks.
Approve the make-or-buy decision and its conditions.

tasks.design: A reusable comparison calculator imports approved requirements and rates from the {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {PROCUREMENT}, with validated file imports where direct access is unavailable. A bounded loop extracts unstructured quote terms from the {DOCS}; deterministic calculations produce scenarios, while the buyer approves outgoing requests and the operations manager approves the sourcing decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Internal costs and supplier offers used different scopes, units and assumptions. Spreadsheet calculations were accessible, but maintaining comparable inputs took specialist work.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable schemas and deterministic scenario calculations are straightforward to build. Bounded document extraction can reduce quote transcription while retaining source references.
tasks.still_hard: Avoidable costs differ from allocated costs. Capacity opportunity costs, supplier reliability, intellectual property and strategic dependence still require judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the cheapest quoted option sacrifices scarce capacity, quality control or future flexibility.

ambition.what: A quarterly make-or-buy review of capacity-constrained components.

tasks.altitude: The estimator can test more demand and capacity scenarios and bring decision thresholds to planning meetings. They gain analytical scope; purchasing commitments and sourcing approval require existing delegated authority.

reach.task: Evaluate production equipment investment against outsourcing.
reach.learn: Discounted cash flow, avoidable cash costs and investment sensitivity.
Disruption scenarios, exposure limits and mitigation costs.

evidence.claim: Transporeon checks freight invoices against agreed rates, supporting deterministic rate comparison as an adjacent capability.
Make-or-buy scenario calculations and bounded quote extraction are proposed applications; the digest contains no direct make-or-buy case.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are unvalidated planning estimates.

assumptions: This baseline uses manufactured components; service and construction comparisons need different input templates.
Supplier waiting time is excluded from active task-time shares.
Internal cost and quote data can be compared at a defined quantity, quality and delivery scope.
No purchase order or supplier contract is created by the comparison tool.
unknowns: Are production routes, labour standards and capacity plans current?
Which overheads are avoidable for the decision horizon?
Who may request quotes and approve sourcing changes?
Are supplier documents permitted in an approved model-processing environment?
Does using labour data require employee consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: Which quote formats can be handled with structured imports alone?
Which assumptions have most often reversed previous make-or-buy recommendations?
How should the calculator represent bottleneck capacity and minimum order quantities?
new_work: Review extracted exclusions and unusual commercial terms.
Maintain cost formulas, currency dates and scenario assumptions.
Compare realised costs with approved sourcing assumptions.

tasks.short: Produce periodic project cost statements, explain variances and release approved reporting packs.

steps.what: Export posted project costs for the reporting period.
Collect open commitments, approved changes, progress and forecast updates.
Reconcile actuals, commitments, accruals and forecast against the approved budget.
Resolve missing postings, disputed accruals and unexplained project variances with cost owners.
Prepare cost statements, supporting schedules and variance commentary.

loop.input: Deterministically calculated report tables and source-linked explanations confirmed by cost owners.
loop.output: Short variance commentary attached to the generated cost statement.
loop.check: Validate every amount against the frozen dataset; require source references for explanations and controller approval before release.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per report; failed checks use factual templates and flag missing explanations.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations and formatting are deterministic. A bounded loop helps condense varied free-text explanations without inventing causes.

steps.what: Review material movements, unresolved exceptions and commentary; approve the report for release.
Distribute the approved report to the authorised internal recipients.
File the released report and its supporting evidence.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles period snapshots from the {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT} and {PROJECT}, then generates statements in the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} routes exceptions and controller approval; a bounded loop drafts source-linked commentary, and approved release automatically preserves the evidence pack and notifies recipients through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Period cut-offs, commitments and project updates were assembled from separate sources. Reusable report templates did not remove reconciliation and explanation work.
tasks.enabler_now: Validated imports, deterministic financial checks and document generation can cover the repeatable work. A small model loop can summarise confirmed explanations without calculating financial figures.
tasks.still_hard: Late costs, disputed progress, accrual estimates and optimistic forecasts cannot be resolved from transaction records alone.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge a plausible-looking forecast and identify when reported progress hides a likely cost overrun.

ambition.what: A weekly forecast-at-completion exception review for active projects.

tasks.altitude: The estimator spends reporting time on exceptions and discussions with project owners. They can propose earlier forecast interventions; budget and report approval rights do not change automatically.

reach.task: Update project forecasts from cost and progress movements.
reach.learn: Forecast drivers, contingency treatment and scenario comparison.
Cut-off rules, evidence standards and accrual reversals.

evidence.claim: Periodic financial statements can combine deterministic reconciliation, report generation and controlled release; no direct estimator reporting case is supplied.
The digest documents a report containing non-existent sources, supporting source checks for generated commentary.
Remaining effort and build ranges are planning hypotheses requiring validation over representative reporting periods.

assumptions: This baseline covers internal management reporting rather than contractual customer submissions.
Cost owners remain responsible for forecast and variance explanations.
Reports use frozen period snapshots and versioned mappings.
Separate manual archiving disappears because approved release creates the archive.
unknowns: Which statements are management reports and which have contractual or statutory requirements?
How are commitments relieved when invoices are posted?
Who approves accrual estimates and forecast changes?
Which report recipients and retention periods are authorised?
Do source feeds contain employee-level data requiring additional access or consultation controls under national rules?
research_questions: Can native reports supply reliable period snapshots and open commitments?
Which historical periods contain useful tests for late postings, reversals and duplicate commitments?
Can fixed commentary templates cover most reports without a model loop?
new_work: Resolve reconciliation failures and stale source feeds.
Maintain report templates, thresholds and recipient lists.
Monitor releases, retained evidence and reporting revisions.

tasks.short: Study work methods and cost drivers to establish standard hours or identify cost reductions.

steps.what: Define the study question, process boundary, sampling method and success criteria.
Retrieve production, labour, quality and cost records for the selected process.
Observe work cycles and discuss delays, variation and practical constraints with workers.
Clean observations and separate setup, productive time, rework and abnormal interruptions.
Estimate standard hours and compare cost-reduction options with uncertainty and quality effects.
Run an authorised trial and check output, quality, safety and worker feedback.
Approve revised standards or cost changes after reviewing trial evidence and consultation outcomes.
Enter approved standard hours and costs with effective dates and supporting references.

tasks.design: A reusable study register in the {WORKFLOW} links structured observations with validated extracts from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP}; deterministic analysis on the {DATA_PLATFORM} generates study tables and sensitivity results in the {DOCS}. People choose methods, interpret worker explanations and authorise trials and standards; approved changes update the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} with effective dates and evidence links.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each study needed a credible sampling design and local process knowledge. Data preparation and rebuilding calculations consumed time, but software could not establish whether observed work was representative.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable observation forms, import adapters and statistical scripts reduce setup and paperwork. No new inference breakthrough is required, and structured observations avoid a model loop.
tasks.still_hard: Separate sustainable performance from unusual conditions, learning effects and measurement bias. Prove that apparent savings survive changes in product mix without harming quality or workers.
tasks.human_edge: Notice when a measured improvement transfers effort elsewhere, depends on unsustainable work intensity or excludes necessary work.

ambition.what: A post-change validation study that checks realised savings and sustainable standard hours.

tasks.altitude: The estimator spends more time observing work, designing trials and checking whether savings persist. They can lead study design and challenge weak evidence; operational standards still need authorised approval.

reach.learn: Sampling, confounding, uncertainty intervals and causal inference.

reach.task: Translate validated process savings into a forecast.
reach.learn: Volume effects, implementation costs and the difference between released capacity and cash savings.

evidence.claim: Structured observation forms, repeatable calculations and controlled standard updates can support studies; the digest supplies no direct standard-hour study case.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; employee-data use and consultation requirements require assessment against the actual design and national rules.
Build ranges include an initial pilot but exclude long production cycles; remaining-time estimates are planning hypotheses.

assumptions: The study concerns process standards rather than individual worker ranking.
Observations use defined categories; people classify ambiguous interruptions.
Calculations flag unusual observations without automatically discarding them.
Existing trial authorisation and required employee consultation precede operational changes.
The access range allows initial consultation work; national procedures may take longer.
unknowns: Do standard hours affect pay, targets, staffing or individual evaluations?
What employee consultation, works-council involvement or agreements apply under national rules?
What GDPR lawful basis, retention period and assessment requirements apply to the intended observations?
Can study records use process-level or pseudonymised data?
Are sufficiently representative production cycles available during the pilot?
Who may authorise trials and approve standard changes?
research_questions: Which sampling method captures product mix, setup variation and learning effects?
Which existing standard calculations can be reused without custom development?
What follow-up period distinguishes sustained savings from temporary improvements?
new_work: Maintain observation categories and analytical methods.
Review data-quality flags and document inclusion decisions.
Keep consultation, trial and approval evidence.
Check realised savings and standard-hour drift after implementation.
Maintain effective dates and reverse superseded standards.

role.altitude: The cost estimator becomes a stronger designer of cost evidence and decision scenarios. Their week shifts toward assumptions, operational discussions and validation; pricing, sourcing, budget and employment-related decisions retain their assigned approvers.
reach: Cost reconciliation and accrual evidence with accountants.
Governed cost datasets with business intelligence analysts.
Controlled cost-reduction trials with data scientists.
skills_to_grow: Configuration, import validation and change control.
Source checking for bounded document extraction and drafting.
Employee-data handling and consultation under applicable national rules.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a reusable cost-decision service that connects estimates, actual costs, sourcing scenarios and verified savings. Start with approved file imports and templates, then add integrations where access and repeat use justify them.
